Law enforcement officials reported that a mobile home was destroyed by the thunderstorm wind gusts and also that four people were injured. An irrigation sprinkler was twisted and two foot diameter trees were uprooted.

The tornado touched down four miles south southeast of Hartley at 1632 CST. The tornado was on the ground for one mile with a maximum path width of fifty yards. The tornado dissipated at 1636 CST. No damage or injuries were reported as the tornado remained over open country.

The public reported wind damage to her home southwest of Dalhart near U.S. Highway 54. The winds reportedly blew down a basketball hoop and a large trampoline in her yard had blown away. No injuries were reported.
Local law enforcement officials reported numerous power lines down due to thunderstorm winds from Channing to five miles north of Channing. No injuries were reported.
A storm chaser from the Mississippi State University Chase Team estimated the thunderstorm wind gust. There was no damage reported and there were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
A trained spotter reported that the thunderstorm wind gusts blew down tree limbs which were four to six inches in diameter. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed or snapped six power poles four miles north of Channing Texas in Hartley county. There were no reports of injuries or fatalities.

A severe wind gust occurred from a possible dry microburst. There was little evidence of a strong storm on radar but there was a cloud deck around 9,000 feet. No known damage occurred from this severe wind gust.
Multiple severe wind gusts were measured at the mesonet site located 12 miles southwest of Dalhart. These gusts ranged from 59mph to 63mph starting around 1525 CDT and lasted through 1535 CDT.
The peak downburst wind gust of 60 mph occurred at 1821CDT with 2 additional gusts of 58 mph shortly after.

Severe wind gusts occurred at the Dalhart 12SW mesonet site from a likely anvil gust from a nearby thunderstorm. The mesonet site initially gusted to 61mph at 1949CDT, had its peak gust of 86mph at 1950CDT, and continued to gust to 79mph and 74mph through 1952CDT.
The first severe wind gust occurred at 2007CDT. The peak gust of 61mph occurred at 2012 CDT at the mesonet site located 12 miles southwest of Dalhart.
